title: Senior Technical Account Manager
description:
Afterpay is transforming the way people shop and pay, giving consumers greater flexibility and control over their finances while helping merchants connect with customers and grow their businesses. Founded in Australia in 2014, Afterpay has grown into a globally recognized leader in Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL), empowering millions of consumers to shop with confidence through a simple, transparent payment experience.

As part of Block’s global ecosystem, Afterpay works alongside Cash App, Square, and other financial products to make commerce and financial services more accessible. Together, we're building innovative solutions that connect consumers and businesses, creating more opportunities for people to participate in the economy.

 

The Role

Block is looking for a Senior Technical Account Manager to support our Afterpay and Cash App merchants across Australia. This team keeps merchants healthy and growing through post-sales technical partnership that protects performance, surfaces opportunity, and drives commercial outcomes.

You will serve as a trusted technical partner to our largest merchants, sitting at the intersection of product, engineering, solutions engineering, GTM, and merchant success. You will combine deep product and technical expertise with commercial acumen to proactively enable merchants - not just resolve issues - ensuring they are healthy, growing, and fully leveraging Afterpay and Cash App Pay capabilities.

This is a hands-on technical role. You will use HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to analyze and creatively solve integration issues on merchant websites and in-store terminals, while partnering cross-functionally to support feature and product adoption at scale. You will translate merchant business needs into technical solutions that deliver measurable commercial outcomes.

In this role, you will report to Block's Global Technical Account Management Lead.

 

You Will

Identify and act on post-sales growth opportunities within your merchant portfolio, partnering with Account Management to grow GPV and feature adoption to deliver measurable commercial outcomes

Provide education to merchants, partners, and internal teams on Cash App Pay and Afterpay features, and deliver quarterly technical reviews connecting integration health to commercial performance

Partner with Solutions Engineering to ensure seamless pre-sales to post-sales handoffs and collaborate on expansion opportunities

Work cross-functionally with Account Management, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, and Engineering to provide technical and operational solutions that improve the merchant experience

Partner with Product and Engineering to represent the merchant voice and frame feature requests with commercial impact

Proactively manage new product life cycles in conjunction with Product and Engineering teams to facilitate merchant adoption

Lead integration health monitoring - conduct regular health checks using defined KPIs, perform root-cause analysis, implement preventative measures, and promote standardization across merchant implementations

Leverage HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to assess and creatively solve integration issues on merchant websites and in-store terminals

Maintain comprehensive integration documentation following established templates

Operate within and contribute to the team's established operating rhythm, including regular merchant health reporting, portfolio reviews, and performance measurement against defined KPIs

Document challenges and blockers encountered to share learnings with other Technical Account Managers in stand-ups and status check-in calls

Participate in on-call incident response rotation with SLA adherence, contributing to end-to-end incident management including RCA delivery and senior leadership communication

Leverage AI and automation tools to improve efficiency in merchant analysis, issue detection, documentation, and portfolio management

Qualifications

We know that no single candidate will meet every qualification listed below. If this role excites you and you see yourself in most of these, we encourage you to apply.

Senior-level experience in account management, customer success, or a client-facing technical role within payments, fintech, or e-commerce

Prior hands-on technical experience in Solutions Engineering, Partner Engineering, Technical Consulting, or software development

Experience managing and growing enterprise accounts, including identifying expansion opportunities and driving commercial outcomes

Solid understanding of payments infrastructure, APIs, integrations, and e-commerce platforms, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences

Proficiency in JavaScript, HTML, and CSS; comfortable assessing and debugging integration issues across e-commerce and POS platforms

SQL and the ability to leverage it for data analysis and troubleshooting

Experience with monitoring tools (Datadog, SumoLogic) for proactive issue detection and portfolio health oversight

Familiarity with platform management processes: environments, testing, release management, and deployments

Strong commercial acumen and ability to balance client advocacy with company objectives

Experience engaging with C-suite and VP-level stakeholders, translating technical insights into business-relevant recommendations

Strong written and verbal communication skills for engaging stakeholders at all levels 

Practical, hands-on experience using AI tools in a professional context with the ability to critically evaluate AI-generated outputs

Direct experience with buy-now-pay-later (BNPL), payment processing, or merchant acquiring is a plus

Background in incident management is a plus

title: Customer Support Officer — Graduate Opportunity
description:
Brighter Together

Our mission is to make consumer energy resources affordable and accessible for everyone.

Brighte is building the platform to enable and accelerate the energy transition by making it affordable, easy, and less risky to buy and sell energy equipment.

Founded by Katherine McConnell, Brighte is a fast-growing business with a strong focus on sustainability, innovation and putting people first. We’re proud to have been recognised as an AFR Sustainability Leader in the Banking and Finance category and to have won the inaugural Sustainability Award at the Affies.

Looking to take your first step into the corporate world?

Have you recently completed, or are you about to complete, your tertiary studies? Are you looking for an opportunity to build your career in a supportive and fast-growing business?

Join Brighte as a Customer Support Officer and gain valuable experience in a professional environment while developing your communication, problem-solving, and customer service skills.

Your manager will support your development through regular training and mentorship sessions tailored to your career goals. We don’t expect you to stay in this role forever; we want to help you build the skills and confidence to grow with Brighte.

What will you do?

As a Customer Support Officer, you’ll support customers throughout their application process and help make their experience as simple and positive as possible.

Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:

Making and taking inbound and outbound customer calls

Responding to general customer enquiries

Supporting customers through their application process

Assisting with account enquiries and updates

Recording accurate customer information in our CRM

Processing payments and documenting payment arrangements

Assisting with basic application or IT-related troubleshooting

Supporting requests relating to withdrawals and cancellations

Working towards agreed customer service targets and service levels

You’ll be part of a supportive team of Customer Support Officers locally, working alongside team members overseas.

What will you bring?

You don’t need years of corporate experience or a specific degree to be successful in this role. We’re looking for someone with the right attitude, a willingness to learn and a genuine interest in helping customers.

You’ll bring:

A recently completed or nearly completed tertiary qualification

Some customer service experience, gained through hospitality, retail, contact centre work or a similar environment

Strong verbal and written communication skills

Confidence speaking with different types of people

Empathy, patience and the ability to stay calm in challenging situations

A proactive and positive approach to learning

Strong attention to detail and accurate data entry skills

The ability to follow processes and work towards targets

Basic problem-solving skills and confidence using technology

Your degree can be in any discipline. We’re more interested in your potential, customer service mindset, and enthusiasm for taking the first step in your career.

What’s in it for you?

Structured training and ongoing mentorship

Clear opportunities to develop your career with Brighte

Flexible working arrangements and a hybrid work model

The autonomy to work from home or from our Sydney office

An office located five minutes from Wynyard Station

Free lunch every Tuesday

Regular social activities, including our Thursday social events

Snacks, fresh fruit and drinks available in the office

End-of-trip facilities with towel service and hair dryers

Anniversary leave

Potential eligibility to participate in our Employee Share Option Plan

Our office days are Tuesday to Thursday, with Monday and Friday available as remote working days.

Our hiring process

At Brighte, we use AI every day, and we’re looking for people who are curious about how technology can improve the way we work.

As part of our hiring process, all roles include an assessment designed to understand how you think and how you use AI in practice. There’s no right tool — while we use Claude, you can use whichever tool you’re most comfortable with. We’ll provide more information during the recruitment process.

Towards the end of the process, successful candidates will be required to complete reference and background checks, including police, anti-money laundering, and bankruptcy checks.

If you’re ready to take your first step into the corporate world and build your career with Brighte, we’d love to hear from you.

title: Senior Collections and Claims Specialist
description:
Senior Collections & Claims Specialist
About Brighte
Our mission is to make consumer energy resources affordable and accessible for everyone.
Brighte is building the platform to enable and accelerate the energy transition by making it easier, more affordable, and less risky to buy and sell energy equipment.
We’re a purpose-led, fast-growing business focused on sustainability, innovation and putting people first. In 2025, Brighte was named an AFR Sustainability Leader in the Banking and Finance category and won the inaugural Sustainability Award at the Affies.
About the role
As a Senior Collections & Claims Specialist, you’ll manage complex arrears, collections, and account dispute matters across a diverse portfolio of customer and vendor accounts.
This is a role for someone who can look beyond an overdue balance to understand what is driving the issue. You’ll investigate matters that may involve financial hardship, incomplete or delayed work, installation concerns, property damage, defective goods, disputed services or unresolved vendor performance issues.
Working closely with customers, vendors, and internal teams, you’ll assess each situation, determine the appropriate path forward, and negotiate sustainable outcomes and recover outstanding debt where appropriate.
What you’ll do
Manage a portfolio of early, late-stage and escalated arrears
Conduct proactive inbound and outbound contact with customers, vendors and internal stakeholders
Investigate the underlying causes of arrears, claims and non-payment
Review contracts, invoices, completion records, correspondence, photographs, reports and payment history
Establish facts, assess responsibility and determine appropriate next steps
Investigate claims relating to incomplete or delayed work, installation concerns, property damage, defective goods, disputed services and vendor performance
Negotiate payment arrangements, settlements, credits, corrections and other approved resolutions
Ensure disputed amounts and claims are appropriately reviewed before progressing through collections
Monitor open claims, disputes, repayment arrangements and agreed actions
Identify signs of financial distress, insolvency risk, vendor underperformance and potential credit loss
Prepare assessments and recommendations for complex, high-priority or non-standard cases
Escalate matters to Credit, Risk, Complaints, Legal, Vendor Management or external recovery channels where appropriate
Apply hardship practices when customers are experiencing personal, medical, family, employment or financial difficulty
Recognise and respond appropriately to vulnerable customer circumstances, including family violence, serious illness, bereavement and financial abuse
Assess hardship requests and identify suitable support options, including deferrals, reduced repayments, extensions and structured arrangements
Ensure decisions are fair, reasonable, appropriately documented and consistent with regulatory and internal requirements
Provide guidance to colleagues on hardship, vulnerable customer and responsible collections matters
Process approved account adjustments, reconciliations, credit memos and minor balance write-offs
Maintain accurate records of contact, evidence reviewed, decisions, claims, disputes and account activity
Contribute to arrears reduction, recovery performance, quality assurance, reporting and process improvement initiatives
What you’ll bring
At least five years’ experience in consumer or commercial credit, collections, financial services, claims management or a related field
Demonstrated experience managing business customer arrears, claims and account disputes
Experience supporting customers experiencing hardship or vulnerability
Strong knowledge of collections strategy, dispute resolution and repayment negotiations
Experience investigating non-payment arising from vendor performance, service delivery issues, disputed transactions or customer complaints
The ability to review information, establish facts, assess responsibility and make sound decisions
Strong negotiation, communication and influencing skills
High emotional intelligence, empathy and resilience
Excellent attention to detail and case documentation skills
The ability to manage competing priorities, sensitive matters and complex escalations
Experience using collections, CRM, account management, claims or credit systems
A commercially aware, customer-conscious and solutions-focused approach
Confidence managing difficult conversations, claims and disputed matters
A calm, professional and accountable approach under pressure
Why join Brighte?
At Brighte, you’ll join a purpose-led business helping make the transition to cleaner energy more affordable and accessible.
You’ll work with collaborative teams across Credit, Risk, Legal, Complaints, Vendor Management, Sales and Customer Support, with the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on both customer outcomes and business performance.
You’ll also have access to:
Flexible working arrangements and a hybrid work model
A collaborative Sydney CBD office
Regular team events and social activities
Free lunch every Tuesday
Snacks, fresh fruit and drinks in the office
End-of-trip facilities
Anniversary leave
Potential eligibility to participate in our Employee Share Option Plan
If you’re an experienced collections and claims professional who brings sound judgement, empathy and a practical approach to complex account matters, we’d love to hear from you.

What you’d be doing in this role
As Canva scales change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

Tech & Product Finance owns the economics of Canva's technical engine, the infrastructure, cloud, compute, GPU and AI investments that power our products and increasingly define our cost base and margin profile. As Canva becomes an AI-native company, these are the fastest-growing and most strategically important lines on the P&L.

Within that, the Technology & Infrastructure team owns the finance seat around how Canva is built and run: the compute, storage and infrastructure that keeps the product running for hundreds of millions of users. Hosting is the single biggest cost lever we steward, and it's one of the fastest-moving: new AI workloads, new negotiation cycles and new savings mechanisms show up almost every quarter. We partner closely with Infra, Platform, Procurement and FinOps leadership to make sure every dollar of hosting spend is understood, forecast well and actively optimised.

Hosting is getting more complex as workloads scale with AI and organic growth, chargeback rolls out and new negotiation cycles come up. This role is the hybrid finance analyst and data analyst that keeps the spend understood, trusted and well forecasted. You'll sit alongside AI and non-AI hosting spend analysts, owning the data layer that both lean on, and partnering with Accounting and technical accounting on the methodologies that split hosting spend across the P&L. Your work gives Finance Business Partners the confidence to lift the numbers straight into strategic analysis, without worrying whether the data holds up. If you enjoy cloud cost data and turning complex data sets into something people can action and confidently rely on, this role is for you.
At the moment, this role is focused on:
You'll get the hosting data reconciled across all our centralised cloud hosting vendor bill line items, so our AI and non-AI FP&A partners can confidently take the numbers and focus on strategic analysis, knowing the data is sound.
You'll own the R&D reclass (COGS vs non-COGS) and free reclass (AI vs non-AI) methodologies in the Anaplan hosting model, the classification rules that split hosting spend across the P&L, partnering with Accounting and tech accounting on audit readiness.
You'll own the finance rhythm for admin hosting: monthly close, quarterly Outlooks and the annual AOP, including ProsperOps accruals and tracking, AWS and GCP invoice validation and monthly billing console reconciliations, reclasses, Anaplan actuals and BvA commentary.

You'll need to earn the trust of engineering leaders quickly, help your engineers navigate different technical and organisational environments, and stay close enough to the work to challenge assumptions and shape important technical decisions.
Embedded is still new, so you won't be stepping into a finished playbook. You'll help decide which problems the team takes on, how engagements should work, what great looks like, and how we measure whether Production Engineering is having the impact we intended.
You'll also be responsible for creating an environment where experienced engineers can do their best work: setting direction, building psychological safety, giving direct coaching and helping senior engineers grow their technical and organisational influence.
Looking ahead, this role will help build:
Impact where it matters most: Focus Embedded on the production problems where it can make the biggest difference, build trust with engineering leaders so the team is brought in early, and make that impact visible through measurable outcomes.

A model that scales: Work out how Embedded can run more engagements without losing the technical bar, coaching quality or close partnerships that make the model effective.

Standards worth reusing: Turn lessons from individual engagements into engineering practices, patterns and capabilities that can benefit teams across Canva.

The next generation of leaders: Develop senior engineers and engagement leads who can coach others, lead increasingly complex work and multiply the team's impact.

You’re probably a match:
We'd love to hear from you if you fit one or more of these. You don't need to meet all of them, but the more the better and if you join the team, we're invested in helping you grow.

Experience:
Leading senior engineers: You've led highly experienced software engineers and technical leads through complex or ambiguous work, and know how to coach people operating with significant autonomy.

Production exposure: You've worked in software environments where reliability, scalability and production risk genuinely mattered.

Earned authority: You've built trust from a standing start, particularly in environments where influence mattered more than reporting lines.

Cross-org delivery: You've led significant technical initiatives spanning multiple teams or groups, from understanding the problem through to delivering an outcome.

Driving adoption: You've persuaded teams to change how they build or operate software, even when they were busy, skeptical or already had an established way of working.

Engineering leadership: You can communicate complex technical trade-offs to senior stakeholders while creating an environment where engineers can challenge ideas, learn, receive direct feedback and do their best work.

Technical knowledge:
CS fundamentals: A strong grounding in computer science fundamentals, including concurrency, multithreading and data structures.

Language depth: Enough depth in languages such as Go, Python, Java or C++ to engage meaningfully with designs, implementation choices and technical trade-offs.

Systems knowledge: Strong working knowledge of system internals, networking and cloud platforms such as AWS or GCP.

Systems thinking: Comfortable reasoning through ambiguous problems spanning multiple components, teams and constraints, with a strong understanding of system design, architecture and engineering patterns.

Reliability engineering: Familiarity with observability, capacity, failure modes and the operational characteristics of production systems.

Scale and criticality: Experience working in large-scale or high-criticality environments where reliability failures have meaningful consequences for users, systems or the business.

Nice to have:
SRE/PE management: Prior experience leading Site Reliability Engineering, Production Engineering or a closely related function

Infrastructure exposure: Experience with large-scale storage, CDN, networking or distributed infrastructure

Growing technical leaders: A history of developing senior engineers and technical leads who can coach others and take on increasingly complex work

Function-building: Experience helping define the identity, operating model or scope of a technical function while it was still taking shape

About the Group and Team:
Production Engineering sits within Canva's Reliability Platform subgroup, part of the wider Infra supergroup responsible for the foundations Canva's engineering teams build on, including compute, storage, networking, developer experience and reliability.
At more than 250 million monthly active users, Canva's hardest reliability problems increasingly span systems, teams and organisational boundaries. Production Engineering exists to help keep Canva reliable, efficient and predictable as that complexity grows.
It's primarily a software engineering function. Rather than operating systems from the sidelines or papering over problems with process, Production Engineers solve operational challenges through design and code.
The function is split into two teams: Embedded and Core.
Embedded works directly alongside teams across Canva on targeted, long-running engineering engagements. Engineers typically work in small groups, combining senior technical leadership with engineers who can learn from the engagement and help carry that knowledge forward.
Core owns Production Engineering services and works on broader problems that cut across multiple teams or groups. When an Embedded engagement uncovers an idea worth applying more widely, Embedded and Core can work together to turn that learning into reusable capability across Canva.
Embedded is deliberately weighted toward senior technical talent. Production Engineers need to enter unfamiliar problem spaces, understand complex systems quickly and earn credibility with the engineers who already own them.
Because the function is still taking shape, the team is also defining its own identity: where Production Engineering can have the greatest impact, how it partners with other teams, and how individual wins become lasting engineering capability across Canva.

title: Chief People Officer
description:
We’re big believers in the power of IRL, so for most roles we ask Campers to work from their local Culture Amp office an average of 2 days a week to unlock connection, pace and culture together.

Join us on our mission to make a better world of work. 

Culture Amp is the world’s leading employee experience platform, revolutionizing how 25 million employees across more than 6,000 companies create a better world of work. Culture Amp empowers companies of all sizes and industries to transform employee engagement, drive performance management, and develop high-performing teams. Powered by people science and the most comprehensive employee dataset in the world, the most innovative companies including Canva, On, Asana, Dolby, McDonalds and Nasdaq depend on Culture Amp every day.

Culture Amp is backed by leading venture capital funds and has offices in the US, UK, Germany and Australia. Culture Amp has been recognized as one of the world’s top private cloud companies by Forbes and most innovative companies by Fast Company.

For more information visit cultureamp.com .

Why this role, and why now

Our Chief People Officer is moving on after three and a half years. They leave behind a People Experience function that works well: predictable delivery, a capable team, a high bar on senior hiring, and a seat at the table that has been earned and respected.

If you want a CPO role where the function is broken and the mandate is to fix it, this isn't it. If you want one where the function is strong and the question is what a leader can do with that platform, keep reading.

The uncomfortable and energising fact about working here: our customers are HR leaders. What we do internally isn’t separate from what we sell. Our own practices are watched, asked about, and sometimes bought. It’s an incredible opportunity to innovate and create the future of work.

We anticipate there may be interest from current and former customers, and we welcome it! Two things worth being upfront about; applications are visible only to our Talent Acquisition and hiring teams, never to our customer-facing teams. And, being a customer earns you no advantage and no disadvantage. We'll run the same process, set the same bar, and have the same people assessing you.

What you'll own

The role has several dimensions. They are listed in order of weight, and we mean the order.

Run People Experience (PX) well

This is a critical part of the job and the thing that has to be true before anything else matters.

You'll own a strong and coherent function that delivers its cycles well and on time: performance, engagement, compensation, talent acquisition, capability, compliance across four countries. No surprises to the Exec. No escalations arriving at the CEO's desk that should have been resolved two levels down.

The bar we're setting: your deputies own outcomes, not tasks. Executives go to them directly and get good answers. You design the org ahead of the strategy rather than in response to it, so that when the business changes direction the structure is already close to right. Your team respects you, and your senior hires raise the average.

You'll be a trusted sounding board to Caroline and the Exec on structure, senior hires, compensation and the calls that don't have clean answers.

Be credible in the market and with customers

Our customers are your peers. That is a commercial asset, and we want you to use it.

You'll speak at our global events and in the market, join customer conversations, and support Sales and Customer Experience in rooms where a practitioner's view might land differently to a vendor's. Over time we'd like Sales to be asking for you by name and customers backchannelling you for advice on their own problems.

To be clear about the bar: we are not hiring a keynote speaker. You don’t need to be a world-class presenter, and polish is not what we're screening for. You need to be reliably credible on a stage and in a room, with a point of view that is specific to you rather than interchangeable with any other HR leader's. Substance over performance.

Lead on AI, personally

The incumbent Chief People Officer leads AI internally; both the technology itself, and the ways of working that are actively being shaped across that.

Sponsoring AI in name while delegating the substance won't work here. We need someone personally fluent: using these tools in their own work, building things, forming first-hand views. You'll set governance across multiple functions, that enables rather than blocks, and drive genuine adoption and behaviour change across a company with strong AI curiosity.

Done well, Culture Amp's own AI transformation becomes something we can talk about externally, and you're one of the people who can talk about it.

Influence the product

You’ll be leading our internal efforts as Customer Zero: where we are our own first and (sometimes toughest) customer.

You'll run Culture Amp on Culture Amp and give R&D feedback that's worth their time. At its best, your practitioner insight shapes product bets rather than joining the queue of stakeholder requests, and the way we use our own product internally generates narratives and proof points that Sales can use.

What we're looking for:

You've led a people function at scale in a global, multi-country business, ideally through a period of significant change.

You build teams strong enough to make you unnecessary in the operational detail, and you've done it before rather than intending to.

You have judgement about organisations that people seek out: structure, senior talent, when to intervene and when not to.

You're willing to say unpopular things to powerful people early, and you've got the track record to prove it isn't just a line in an interview.

You're personally very capable with AI. You use it in your own work, you've built things with it, and you've set governance that enabled adoption rather than slowed it, including across functions you don't own.

You have a view about the future of work that is yours, and you can credibly defend it in front of an audience of HR leaders.

You're willing to be deployed commercially: joining customer calls, taking the hard practitioner questions Sales can't answer, and speaking at our events. Experience doing this already is a plus, but the appetite matters more. Over time we'd want Sales asking for you by name.

You want to work somewhere your internal practice is externally visible, and you find that motivating rather than exposing.

You've ideally worked in tech or SaaS, which helps with the pace and with the R&D relationship. If you haven't, we're still interested. We care more about whether you've operated at this scale and complexity than the industry you did it in.

 

Perks & Benefits

At Culture Amp, our people are at the heart of our success. We offer competitive pay and a total rewards package designed to support you at work and in life. This includes:

Equity through our Employee Share Option Program, so you can share in our long-term success

Learning programs and coaching to help you thrive and grow

Quarterly refresh days, an extended end-of-year break and a monthly allowance to support your wellbeing and lifestyle

Inclusive parental leave from day one

A MacBook and budget to set up your home workspace, enabling flexibility

Five annual social impact days to to give back to causes that matter to you

Medical insurance coverage for you and your family (Available for US & UK only)

Our rewards are designed to support different needs and life stages, recognising that what matters most can vary from person to person.

Research shows that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds may hesitate to apply if they don’t meet every requirement, but your unique experience matters. If you’re interested in joining us, we strongly encourage you to apply and help us build a more diverse and impactful team.

description:

About the role
As our Demand Generation Lead you will partner with the marketing, product, sales, and customer success teams to turn Dovetail’s strongest product stories, customer proof, and account signals into qualified enterprise pipeline
You’ll own targeted demand programs for new and existing enterprise customers, from audience and offer through to campaign, sales follow-up, and reporting. You’ll work closely with Product Marketing, Growth, Web, Content, Creative, Sales, Customer Success, and Revenue Operations to build programs that create opportunities and help progress complex deals.
This is a senior individual contributor role for a builder. You’ll set direction, run programs yourself, and turn what works into a repeatable demand engine.
Please note this is a full-time in person-first role (in office 4 days a week), working from our Surry Hills HQ.

What you’ll do
Own the enterprise demand plan. Set priority audiences, account segments, offers, campaign calendar, targets, and budget. Keep every program tied to a clear pipeline outcome.

Build integrated campaigns. Turn product launches, customer stories, original research, executive content, webinars, and market moments into coordinated programs across paid media, web, email, events, and sales outreach.

Run account-based marketing programs. Partner with Sales to select accounts, map buying groups, identify account signals, and build the right mix of tailored content, executive engagement, events, and scaled campaigns.

Create expansion demand. Work with Sales and Customer Success to reach new teams, senior buyers, and executive sponsors inside existing enterprise customers. Use product adoption, account activity, customer proof, and new use cases to open expansion opportunities.

Work inside the sales motion. Join pipeline reviews and account planning, give sellers a clear follow-up plan, and use deal feedback to improve targeting, messaging, and programs.

Build, measure, and scale an AI-powered demand engine. Own the tools, workflows, prompts, and automation used to target accounts, produce higher-quality campaigns faster, and measure performance. Partner with Engineering to build beyond off-the-shelf marketing platforms and with Revenue Operations to track results from sales acceptance through closed revenue. Turn what works into repeatable programs, and stop what creates activity without opportunity.

Skills and experience
Taste. A high creative and commercial bar. You can tell what will earn a senior buyer’s attention, explain why, and improve the work until it does.

AI fluency as craft. Hands-on with modern AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT, with examples of workflows, agents, and prompts you have improved over time. You see AI as a system to operate, not a button to press.

A systems and tooling builder. Comfortable owning the demand generation stack end to end and partnering with Engineering and Revenue Operations to ship internal tools, integrations, and automation.

Enterprise pipeline ownership. Experience in B2B SaaS demand generation, account-based marketing, or growth, with a record of creating new-business and expansion pipeline through complex sales cycles.

Strong account-based marketing fundamentals. You know account selection, buying-group research, intent signals, personalization, and how to orchestrate Marketing and Sales around named opportunities.

Hands-on in the weeds. You audit the funnel, build the audience, write the brief, launch the program, and read the results. You do the work, not just direct it.

Commercial fluency. You understand funnel economics and measure success through sales acceptance, opportunity progression, pipeline, and revenue—not clicks or lead volume.

A strong cross-functional collaborator across Sales, Customer Success, Product Marketing, Revenue Operations, Data, Engineering, Creative, Web, and Growth.

Bias to action. You would rather launch a strong program, learn from real account behavior, and iterate than wait for a perfect plan.

About you
You sweat the details. You care about words. You can hold a clear point of view, and stay humble when the evidence changes your mind. You have a clear bias to action and can drive to clear outcomes in ambiguity. You will thrive here if you want to compound your craft with AI, rather than defend a pre-AI way of working.

We hire smart people and look after them well! Here's the deal:
📈 Equity for everyone. Competitive base salary plus options, so every builder is aligned on long-term impact.
🏢 A place to do your best work, wherever you are. Our Sydney office is built for in-person first collaboration. Our US team runs on a flexible remote setup. Either way, you've got what you need.
🤝 Built in connection. Join a Doveclub, bond with your team regularly, and celebrate the small wins, big milestones, and cultural moments with the whole company.
📚 Learn and thrive. Flexible L&D and wellness benefits, choose between a generous $3000 L&D allowance, or up to $1000 on wellness.
🌴 Time to recharge. Four weeks of accrued leave, floating public holidays, and gifted bonus Kit Kat days sprinkled throughout the year.
🌍 Four weeks from anywhere. Up to four weeks a year doing your job from anywhere in the world. Split it up or use it all at once.
🍼 Generous parental leave. We offer 20 weeks for primary caregivers, 12 weeks for secondary caregivers, plus return-to-work support.
🎉 Four weeks at four years. Four years is a long time in tech, and we value loyalty. Take an additional four weeks off to reset and recharge.
🩺 Stellar US benefits. Comprehensive health, dental, vision, 401(k), and more through Sequoia.

title: Senior Manager, APJ Field & Channel Marketing
description:
Role Description

As Senior Manager, APJ Field & Channel Marketing, you will lead the development and execution of Dropbox’s regional marketing strategy across the entire Asia-Pacific and Japan region. You will bring the greatest depth of focus to Dropbox’s Tier 1 markets—Australia/New Zealand, Singapore, Korea, India, and Japan—while building fit-for-market programs for Tier 2 markets including Vietnam, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. Reporting to the Chief Marketing Officer, you will work in close partnership with the Regional VP of Sales to translate business priorities into integrated marketing strategies and campaigns that create pipeline, accelerate opportunities, and support regional sales growth.

This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role at the intersection of field marketing, channel marketing, sales, and Dropbox’s global marketing organization. Field and channel marketing will be equally important as Dropbox evolves toward a hybrid go-to-market model in ANZ and adapts its approach across APJ. You will build the regional marketing plan, manage the regional budget, and measure performance against clear business outcomes. You will also manage and develop our Japan Marketing team, ensuring our regional approach combines consistent strategy and operating discipline with strong local-market relevance.

 

You will be Dropbox Marketing’s senior voice in the region—bringing APJ customer, partner, and market insights into global planning while adapting global campaigns for local audiences. The ideal candidate is a collaborative, commercially minded leader who can move comfortably between executive-level strategy, people leadership, and hands-on campaign execution.

Responsibilities

Develop and own the integrated field and channel marketing strategy for APJ, aligned with regional sales priorities and Dropbox’s global marketing strategy.

Partner closely with the Regional VP of Sales and sales leadership to develop regional and country-level plans that create qualified pipeline, accelerate priority opportunities, and support revenue growth.

Lead the planning and execution of regional marketing programs across field events, executive experiences, account-based initiatives, integrated campaigns, partner and channel activations, webinars, and other locally relevant tactics.

Build an equally strong field and channel marketing motion, balancing direct-to-customer and partner-led investments by market using customer insight, sales priorities, partner opportunity, and performance data.

Lead, coach, and develop the Japan Marketing team by establishing clear goals, operating rhythms, and opportunities for growth while enabling strong local execution.

Build strong relationships with regional sales, partner sales, and channel leaders; create joint plans with priority partners and develop co-marketing programs that extend Dropbox’s market reach and generate partner-sourced or partner-influenced demand.

Translate global campaigns, positioning, and content into regionally relevant programs, partnering with global Campaigns, Product Marketing, Brand, Digital, Communications, Marketing Operations, and other teams.

Own the regional marketing budget, agency and vendor relationships, program calendar, forecasting, and performance reporting; continuously optimize investments based on pipeline impact and ROI.

Establish clear KPIs and operating cadences with Sales and Marketing Operations, including regular planning sessions and business reviews that connect marketing activity to pipeline creation and opportunity progression.

Represent APJ within the global marketing organization, sharing market intelligence, customer and partner feedback, competitive insight, and regional best practices to improve company-wide strategy and execution.

Build a scalable regional marketing playbook that balances consistency across APJ with the distinct needs, cultures, routes to market, and buying behaviors of individual countries.

Travel within the region and internationally as needed to support team leadership, sales planning, partner engagement, and key programs—approximately 20%

Requirements

10+ years of progressive B2B marketing experience, including significant experience in regional, field, demand generation, and/or channel marketing within enterprise software, SaaS, or another technology environment.

Demonstrated experience developing and executing multi-country APJ marketing strategies that produced measurable pipeline and sales impact.

People-management experience, including coaching and developing marketers working across different countries, cultures, or time zones.

Proven ability to operate as a strategic partner to senior sales leaders, translate sales priorities into marketing plans, and build alignment through planning and business reviews.

Experience leading an integrated mix of field and channel programs, including events, account-based programs, partner co-marketing, campaigns, and pipeline-acceleration initiatives.

Strong commercial and analytical skills, including experience managing regional budgets, setting program KPIs, evaluating pipeline contribution, and using performance data to optimize investment.

Excellent executive communication, cross-functional leadership, and influencing skills, with the ability to operate effectively in a global, distributed, and highly collaborative organization.

Preferred Qualifications

Deep familiarity with the APJ technology market, with experience developing differentiated strategies across mature and emerging markets; direct experience in several of Dropbox’s Tier 1 markets is strongly preferred.

Experience in a channel-led or partner-influenced go-to-market model, including co-marketing with resellers, distributors, alliances, or technology partners.

Experience building or evolving a regional marketing function, operating model, or playbook in a growing or changing business.

Strong understanding of enterprise and commercial buying journeys, account-based marketing, opportunity acceleration, and regional event strategy.

Experience working in a Virtual First or similarly distributed global organization.

Awareness: U nderstand yourself and others .

About the role

The best CEO offices in the world do five things: run the leadership team's operating rhythm, speed decisions up, produce analysis that everyone trusts, take on the problems that don't have a home yet, and produce people who go on to run things. Some examples of what this involves:

Produce the operating weekly view of the business that executives in the U.S., Europe and Australia run the company off - revenue, marketing spend and cohort economics across every market reconciled with the finance function of a listed company. You'll know where every figure comes from and defend any of them.

Help run the operating rhythm of the leadership team - the weekly business review, the executive leadership meeting, the monthly global all-hands, the quarterly offsites (the last two: London and New York). Agendas, packs, pre-reads, follow-ups.

Help build the analysis behind the biggest calls we make - group financial forecasts in conjunction with FP&A, repricing models with cohort analyses, stage-gate financial plans, a competitor's launch sized from external data, competitor tracking across different growth channels. 

Write the words the company runs on - the all-hands narrative, the notes flying between Sydney and New York, the write-up when something big changes. Synthesis is the job: compressing complicated materials into things multiple different groups (leaders, all staff, new joiners) can absorb in one pass.

Take the problems that have no home - leading the change of rituals that the leadership partake in, rebuilding the system and execution of our Global Growth teams, integration workstreams, equity and payment models arising from the transaction with Hims & Hers where the tolerance for error is zero. A pricing engine. AI tooling for how the executive team works. A faster way for our global teams to see the same numbers, different capital allocation rituals. You’ll be encouraged to run projects you pitch. 

One thing to know before you apply: This is an intense role working with an intense set of stakeholders who are committed to winning. We also span several time zones: Sydney, London, New York, and California. Some calls land at ~7 AM in Australia while some finish at 11 PM. The trade is responsibility years ahead of your experience, and a rate of learning we think you’ll find incredibly rewarding. 

 

Why should you join Eucalyptus now?

The most rewarding careers come from being in the right place at the right time: The Facebook growth team in 2008, Uber while it was still in a few cities, Airbnb before the sharing economy. The pattern behind them is remarkably consistent: a truly global market, proven product-market fit, tailwinds driving double-digit monthly growth, and bottlenecks that are commercial rather than technical. The hard part is timing: after the model is proven but before the market has priced the upside.

That's where we believe preventative healthcare is right now. GLP-1s are the defining pharmaceutical innovation of our generation, and they've created an addressable market of more than 30% of the population of every country on earth. We're growing >10% month on month in markets that are less than 5% penetrated, and we've watched markets go from launch to nine figures of ARR in under six months. In this role, you’ll be privy to the capital allocation decisions and have exposure to some of the best D2C operators in the world in a truly global category.

Skills and experience

You have 2-3 years of experience working in a high-pressure environment such as consulting (MBB preferred), investment banking, or as an operator in a recent high-growth startup. We're open to other backgrounds, but we operate at the intensity of these types of organisations and are uncompromising on our expectations.

Judgement under ambiguity: You can research a market or topic independently, work out what the unit economics depend on and the WYNTB (‘what you’d need to believe’), as well as landing on a clear, structured go/no-go point of view.

Communication and sharp writing: You write tight theses and clear slide decks. A one-pager an executive can act on without needing a meeting; a tight, coherent thesis; a clean deck. Synthesis is the job.

Commercial & financial modelling: You can build a commercial model from scratch, make your assumptions explicit, and defend them across market sizing, unit economics  (CAC, LTV, payback), and deal structures.

You're genuinely strong with Claude, not just prompting it for first drafts, but using it to automate access to information, stress-test arguments, and build repeatable workflows. You see it as leverage on your thinking, never a replacement for it. The ability to self-serve using Sigma will also be highly valued.

Project management: You've run complex cross-functional workstreams with real accountability on tight deadlines. 

Founder mindset: You operate like a founder and enjoy the hustle of getting things done. You are an example of resilience and ownership - when something breaks, you fix it; you don't wait for others. You want to run something eventually and treat this as the apprenticeship for it.

Behaviours & Attitudes

You act like an owner and lead with humility. 

You’re incredibly curious and enjoy stress testing your thinking and conclusions.

You are low ego and highly coachable.

You're resilient, adaptable, and comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities.

You move fast and can manage yourself to a high standard.

Design rigorous experiments. Own A/B and multivariate testing from hypothesis through to execution, analysis and decision-making.

Turn experiments into decisions. Clearly articulate what worked, what didn't and why, using results to determine what we ship, iterate or stop.

Understand the customer behind the numbers. Combine quantitative data with customer insight to understand intent, friction, trust and the reasons people hesitate or abandon their journey.

Partner with Engineering and Product. Take opportunities from diagnosis through to implementation rather than stopping at recommendations.

Build new conversion journeys. As Juniper expands its product ecosystem, help create and optimise funnels for new products and patient needs.

Experience working with Analytics or Data teams to build robust measurement and attribution frameworks .

Strong customer judgement and an understanding of how UX, messaging, friction and behavioural psychology influence conversion.

Experience working closely with Design, Copy, Engineering and Product to turn hypotheses into shipped experiences.

Strong commercial judgement and an ability to connect individual funnel metrics to broader business outcomes.

Design the contract and compliance framework with Legal: establish contracting standards and templates in partnership with Legal and Compliance, and ensure all products meet Australian labelling and ARTG-compliant requirements, with import duties, customs, and biosecurity obligations managed for inbound product.

Comfortable designing frameworks (supply-risk, contracting standards, sourcing strategy) in partnership with Legal and Compliance, rather than only operating within frameworks others have set.

A self-starter and strong cross-functional partner, able to translate commercial strategy into an aligned category plan and stand up an S&OP cadence from scratch.

Analytical and fluent with cost and margin data; ERP and procurement system experience is advantageous.

title: Legal & Sustainability Associate
description:
Who are we?

Lyka is an Australian founded pet wellness company that’s shaking up an outdated industry and paving the way for happier, healthier pets. Despite medical advancements, animal lifespans are on the decline. Today, the average pet only reaches 37% of their full potential lifespan and statistics have shown us that many suffer from dental disease, cancer, and obesity. Simply put, the status quo is not enough.

As humans, we’ve experienced firsthand the positive impact fresh wholefoods can have on our health and wellbeing, and we believe our furry friends deserve the same. We're on a mission to do just that, starting with nutritionally balanced, wholefood meals delivered direct to doors around Australia. As the world’s most sustainable pet wellness company, we’re putting pets and our planet first - one bowl at a time.

Today, we are proud to share we’ve served 100 million meals to puppers and their parents across Australia, and this is just the beginning. Our vision is to create multiple nutritional products, adding disease prevention meals and supplements, and expand into new markets.

Currently, we have a team of 250+ pet-obsessed people and we're continuing to grow (yes, looking at you!). These carefully selected people are dedicated to building the next generation of technology and products to help empower pet parents to take control over their pet’s wellbeing.

To date, we have raised over $60M in funding from venture capital investors and pet industry insiders, who believe in our mission and ability to drive change in a stagnant industry, providing nutrition that nourishes puppers from the inside out.

Are you ready to shake things up and give pets the life they deserve? Come join our pack!

Our Mission

The time we share with our pets is being cut short. Despite medical advancements, they’re getting sicker earlier. They’re dying prematurely. The industry has it backwards - prioritising treating symptoms instead of addressing the root cause. That’s where we come in.

At Lyka, we take a preventative, holistic and personalised approach to pet care. We look at the full picture, factoring in the diet, lifestyle and environment of each individual animal.

We don’t stop at symptoms, instead we dig for the root cause. We create nutrition plans unique to each pet, because it’s not just about living longer, but living well too.

Our mission is to increase the lifespan of dogs and cats.

The Role

We're looking for a Legal & Sustainability Associate to lead the delivery and ongoing development of Lyka's sustainability strategy, reporting and initiatives, while supporting a broad range of general in-house legal matters.

Our ideal candidate is a lawyer admitted to practice in Australia with a strong interest in environmental sustainability, ESG and responsible business - you don't need to be an established expert, just the curiosity and initiative to build that expertise quickly. Equally, if you're not a lawyer but bring strong sustainability, ESG or responsible-business experience and are comfortable working closely with our legal function, we'd love to hear from you.

What you’ll do:
Lead the delivery and ongoing development of Lyka's sustainability strategy, metrics and targets, monitoring performance and reporting regularly to leadership and the Board.
Support general in-house legal matters, including contract review, legal and regulatory research, compliance and practical legal guidance.
Build expertise across environmental laws, regulations and reporting frameworks relevant to Lyka's operations and value chain, and identify emerging legal and sustainability-related risks and legislation to support risk management.
Manage sustainability reporting, data collection and compliance requirements.

Simply put, the status quo is not enough.

As humans, we’ve experienced firsthand the positive impact fresh wholefoods can have on our health and wellbeing, and we believe our furry friends deserve the same. title: SHEQ Associate
description:
About Lyka:

Lyka was founded in 2018 by  Anna Podolsky , inspired by her dog,  Lyka , who was suffering from chronic health issues despite being on “premium” kibble. Together with  Gabriel Guedes  (COO) and  Dr. Matthew Muir  (Integrative Veterinarian), they built Lyka from the ground up with one core belief:  better food can radically improve a pet’s healthspan and quality of life .

Lyka’s meals are  vet-formulated and gently cooked from real food ingredients . Delivered via a flexible subscription model, Lyka meals have driven remarkable improvements for tens of thousands of customers, supporting gut health, reducing intolerances, improving energy and mobility, and even promoting hair growth.

What began as home-cooked meals has since scaled into one of  Australia’s fastest-growing consumer companies , a vertically integrated, tech-enabled brand that is transforming pet health nationwide.

Lyka now operates from two offices,  Sydney (HQ) and Melbourne , with three state-of-the-art food production facilities (two in Sydney, one in Melbourne) and a growing national footprint.

At Lyka, we’re not just selling pet food, we’re pioneering a new standard of wellness for pets. With strong product-market fit, deep customer love, and a track record of rapid growth, we’re now entering our most ambitious chapter yet: building a generational brand and category-defining business with global impact.

About the role:
This is a supporting and enabling role at heart, less about enforcing standards from the sidelines, and more about teaching, coaching and mentoring the frontline and operational teams who make our product, so that safety, environmental and food safety practice becomes second nature across the network.

You'll work closely with the SHEQ Manager, stepping in as backup when needed, and you'll be the person who digs into root cause when something falls short of standard, then drives the corrective and preventative action that stops it happening again.

Alignment with FSSC 22000 and Prime Safe sits at the centre of the role, and you'll play a genuine part in building and continuously improving Lyka's Food Safety Management System as our sites mature.

What you will do:
You'll lead the rollout of HACCP and GMP compliant quality standards on site, working from initial certification through to internationally recognised standards as our facilities grow, and you'll embed frontline SHEQ activity that every Pack member is expected to take part in.
Quality control runs through the whole operational process on your watch, receivals, product preparation, manufacturing, storage, packaging, fulfilment and dispatch, and you'll be inspecting equipment, testing product and monitoring facility cleanliness to keep us meeting international food safety requirements.
You'll set and monitor supplier requirements for raw materials and intermediate products, track and investigate customer complaints and non-conformances through to resolution with the relevant teams, and keep accurate, fully traceable quality records throughout.
Documentation is a real part of the job too, building out new SHEQ processes and creating the training materials that help the standard stick.
Requirements
What we expect from you:
You'll bring at least two years of QA/QC experience in a food manufacturing environment, ideally including meat production and cooking, along with a solid grounding in ISO quality systems, HACCP and GMP, experience with FSSC 22000 will put you ahead of the pack.
Formal HACCP and GMP certification is expected, and certification in other systems is a bonus.
Beyond the technical grounding, we need someone with a genuine eye for detail, strong written and verbal communication, and the relationship-building skills to work effectively with internal teams and external clients and service providers alike.
You'll be comfortable across multiple sites, confident using the Microsoft Office suite and picking up new systems, and ready to flex your hours when an emergency calls for it.
Above all, we're looking for someone self-motivated and reliable, genuinely committed to human safety, food safety and the environment, who can hold their ground on standards while still being a proactive, easy team player to work alongside.

Megaport is the global leader in Network as a Service (NaaS), and has transformed the way businesses connect to the cloud, data centers, and each other. We’re publicly listed on the Australian Stock Exchange and partnered with the biggest names in tech like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Oracle, IBM, and more. Headquartered in Brisbane with a crew of over 600 people spread across Asia-Pacific, Europe, and the Americas, our employees enjoy an environment that is collaborative, supportive, and (actually) fun.
 
Our Team Culture
We’re a team of problem solvers, pixel pushers, code slingers, and cloud fanatics. Culture is more than a poster on the wall here – collaboration beats hierarchy, curiosity fuels our growth, and everyone’s voice matters. We take our work seriously, but not ourselves. We work across time zones to execute on our global vision, trust each other to get things done, and never compromise our values for commercial gain. Most importantly, we place our customers at the center of everything we do.
 
We’re committed to increasing representation in the tech industry and welcome applicants from all backgrounds. Don’t meet every requirement? That’s okay. If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply.

Your Role 
As Financial Accountant within our Capex team, you will oversee the end-to-end management of capital expenditure (capex), fixed assets, and inventory across our global network. This role plays a key part in ensuring capitalised wages, fixed asset and intangible registers, and inventory ledgers are accurately maintained and compliant. You will also drive continuous improvement and automation of related systems, processes, and controls.
Additionally, you will have the opportunity to work closely with other departments including Sales, Operations, Procurement and Engineering. The ideal candidate will be able to demonstrate proven experience in applying IFRS accounting standards, have a strong understanding of financial principles, and possess an analytical edge to provide meaningful analysis and reporting to management. You will also drive continuous improvement and automation of related systems, processes, and controls.
What You’ll Be Doing Manage capital work in progress through to asset capitalisation upon project completion

Maintain fixed asset, intangible asset, and inventory registers across multiple regions in coordination with cross-functional teams

Partner with stakeholders to track and communicate the status of current and upcoming capital projects

Develop, implement, and maintain accounting policies and procedures for capitalisation, fixed assets, and inventory management

Act as the key finance lead for wage capitalisation

Prepare asset schedules, including movement analysis for half-year and year-end financial reporting

Support external audit, addressing fixed asset and inventory related queries

Develop commercial understanding of key supplier contracts to inform asset management decisions

Contribute to annual budgeting and rolling forecasts with capex inputs

Prepare ad hoc reports and analysis as needed What We Are Looking For Minimum 2 years experience in a similar role

CPA, CA, or equivalent qualification (or currently studying toward one)

Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet tight deadlines

Strong understanding of financial management in a technology-driven environment

Exceptional attention to detail

Strong written and verbal communication skills

The Regional Alliances Manager - Distribution & Emerging Partners is the strategic catalyst for growing Okta's distribution channel and a new network of emerging partners across Australia and New Zealand. You will own Okta's distribution relationships in ANZ and build a new segment of emerging partners: boutique enterprise consultancies, digital transformation firms and AI builders.

About 80% of your focus is distribution. The other 20% is bringing emerging partners into Okta's partner program and helping them mature, using distribution to scale that motion. You will report to the Director of Partners & Alliances, ANZ.

Own forecasting, pipeline development and revenue targets for partner-sourced and partner-influenced business through distribution and emerging partners.

Give our Commercial sales team scale in ANZ through distributors and partners.

Onboard and enable 6 new emerging partners within 12 months, and move each along the program's maturity path: certified sales, pre-sales and delivery staff; first registered deal; first closed deal; repeatable pipeline.

Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support partner-led customer engagements and remove blockers to execution.

title: Head of Product, PrezzeePay
description:
Prezzee is a global leader in digital gifting and payments, having sold over 140 million gift cards through partnerships with more than 1,500 brands and serving over 6 million customers worldwide. Our mission is to change lives through the power of giving — leveraging borderless payment technology and innovative digital solutions to help people connect and create memorable moments that truly matter.

 

Prezzee is looking for a seasoned product leader to own and elevate PrezzeePay as a core growth engine for the business. As Head of Product, PrezzeePay, you’ll own the vision, strategy, roadmap and end-to-end performance of the payments and issuing value stream. By working across the business and external partners, you’ll turn customer problems, business priorities and market opportunities into clear product strategies and measurable outcomes.

 

This is a senior strategic and operational leadership role where you’ll make the calls that shape what we build, why we build it and how we deliver it.

 

What You’ll Do

Define the long-term customer-led and data-driven strategy for PrezzeePay and own value-stream OKRs.

Build and manage a multi-quarter roadmap balancing customer value, commercial impact, technical sustainability and operational efficiency.

Lead customer and partner discovery, using behavioural data, analytics, research and experimentation to drive product decisions.

Identify new payment use cases, growth opportunities, business models and partnerships.

Own GTM strategy and partner closely with Marketing, Commercial, Partnerships, Operations, Risk and Compliance to launch and scale new capabilities.

Build strong relationships across schemes, processors, issuers and strategic partners.

Own prioritisation, business cases, ROI analysis and investment decisions across the value stream.

Lead multiple squads and drive alignment across Product, Engineering, UX, Data and other functions.

Own delivery, proactively managing dependencies, risks and blockers to ensure predictable outcomes.

Establish PrezzeePay as a growth product -not simply payments infrastructure.

 

What You Bring

10+ years’ experience in product strategy, product management, portfolio leadership or program delivery within technology-driven organisations.

Strong experience leading multiple squads or large multidisciplinary teams.

Deep understanding of payments, issuing, prepaid open-loop and closed-loop cards, schemes, processors and program management.

Proven experience developing customer- and data-led product strategies and multi-quarter roadmaps.

Strong commercial acumen, including business cases, forecasting, modelling and ROI analysis.

Experience leading complex GTM initiatives and working with external partners.

Strong decision-making skills and the ability to make clear trade-offs in ambiguous environments.

Exceptional stakeholder management and executive-level communication.

Experience working with distributed and global teams.

 

Your Strengths

Strategic thinker with strong customer and commercial instincts.

Decisive, accountable and comfortable making tough prioritisation calls.

Outcome-driven, with a bias towards measurable impact over activity.

Analytical and data-literate, using evidence to drive decisions.

Influential leader who can align and galvanise cross-functional teams.

Comfortable with ambiguity and able to bring clarity to complex challenges.

Collaborative communicator who builds trust across teams and stakeholders.

 

Why Join Prezzee?

This is an opportunity to shape a strategically important product and help make payments a core growth engine for Prezzee.You’ll have the autonomy and influence to define the future of PrezzeePay, working with talented global teams to build scalable payments and issuing capabilities, accelerate partner and program launches, and unlock new customer and commercial opportunities.

 

At Prezzee, Where We Don’t Just Work – We Innovate, Collaborate, And Shape The Future Of Digital Giving. As Part Of Our Dynamic Team, You’ll Contribute To a Global Company’s Growth While Enjoying a Flexible, Supportive, And Inclusive Work Environment.

Beyond team development, you will serve as a critical organisational anchor in our Sydney office, bridging the gap between global Customer Success and our local Product and Engineering teams to influence our broader product roadmap.
This role requires a minimum of 3 days per week in our Sydney office.

Key Responsibilities:

Commercial Growth, Enterprise Strategy & Forecasting
Enterprise Revenue Ownership: Own the aggregate Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) targets for the APAC region, including Gross Revenue Retention (GRR) and Net Revenue Retention (NRR).
Advanced Deal Architecture: Navigate highly complex enterprise account plans, mapping out multi-stakeholder corporate structures, identifying white-space expansion opportunities, and managing complex Master Services Agreements (MSAs) and contracts.
Leadership Autonomy: Take full ownership of regional forecasting and deal strategy, shifting operational weight off senior regional leadership to independently run the commercial engine.
Executive Presence: Build high-credibility relationships at the executive level for our largest clients, while remaining equally comfortable engaging with teams on construction and survey sites.

Operational Strategy & Proactive Planning

Predictive Portfolio Management: Establish a comprehensive strategy for APAC’s existing customer book, proactively modeling long-term growth vectors and identifying attrition risks before they materialise.
Data-Driven Capacity Planning: Dynamically evaluate and assign team portfolios based on customer complexity, deal size, and account health rather than basic volume.
Escalation Architecture: Act as the ultimate regional escalation point for at-risk enterprise accounts, deploying sophisticated objection-handling and recovery strategies to restore client trust.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Product Bridging

Product & Engineering Sync: Act as the primary, on-the-ground CS bridge to the Sydney-based P&E teams, synthesising regional data trends into highly structured, prioritised product feedback that drives global roadmap alignment.
Cross-Functional Optimisation: Partner with Sales, Marketing, and Support leaders to ensure frictionless post-sales handoffs and unified messaging for enterprise-tier accounts.

Strategic Team Leadership & Active Coaching

Commercial Capabilities Coaching: Transition the management culture from administrative facilitation to deep professional coaching. Conduct granular, tactical coaching sessions (shadowing calls, reviewing commercial copy) to elevate the team’s negotiation, value-based selling, and contract-savviness capabilities.
High-Accountability Culture: Drive individual development plans, rigorous performance standards, and proactive career pathing to retain and scale high-potential talent within the APAC team.

5+ years of direct people management experience explicitly leading high-performing Customer Success or Account Management teams in a B2B SaaS environment.
10+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, or commercial revenue-generating roles.
Proven track record of personally managing, expanding, and renewing complex enterprise accounts with high annual contract values, multiple corporate stakeholders, and rigorous contract/MSA requirements.
Exceptional structural knowledge of SaaS commercial models, revenue forecasting metrics, and advanced commercial negotiation strategies.
Demonstrated success operating independently in ambiguous, high-growth environments to build business strategies from the ground up.
Strategic Revenue Management: Proven expertise in driving Net Revenue Retention (NRR) through accurate forecasting and the use of CRM / CSM tools (Gainsight, Salesforce, HubSpot or similar) to manage team performance and scale revenue impact.

Familiarity with geospatial data, construction workflows, civil engineering, or hardware-enabled software platforms.
